goalTree.description:
Two projects, adopted, and now to be integrated: pettycash is brought into invoicer. Each was written before, by
  someone else, and each already builds and passes its own tests. In their own words, from their READMEs:

    "invoicer -- Invoices in one currency: money with its currency, billing periods, invoice lines and their total."
    "pettycash -- A petty-cash book: amounts in cents, expenses with a payee, a category and whether they are billable,
    totals by category and period."

  The build has two modules: pettycash/ is the pettycash project, invoicer/ is the invoicer project and depends on
  pettycash. The root pom.xml only lists the two modules. Both projects' tests are in their modules' src/test/java.

  How the two fit together was decided in a merge session; those decisions are among the obligations of this goal.

  The integration wanted, with the focus on billing: the billable expenses of a petty-cash book become the lines of an
  invoice.

  - BillableExpenses.lines(ExpenseBook book, Period period, String currency) returns, in the book's order, one LineItem
    per billable expense whose date the period contains (its first and last day included): the payee as the
    description, quantity 1, and the expense's amount as a Money of the same cents in the given currency. The list
    cannot be modified. Period, LineItem and Money are invoicer's; ExpenseBook and Expense are pettycash's.
  - BillableExpenses.invoice(String number, Period period, String currency, ExpenseBook book) returns a new Invoice with
    that number, period and currency, holding those lines (an invoice without lines totals zero in its currency).

  The specification is BillableExpensesSpecTest, InvoicerSpecTest and PettyCashSpecTest in src/test/java:
  BillableExpensesSpecTest says exactly what the integration must do and fails until the code provides it; the other
  two are each project's own specification and keep passing.

  OBJECTIVE: every test in BillableExpensesSpecTest passes, and the whole suite passes.

  The classes to change are BillableExpenses -- it does not exist yet: create it under invoicer/src/main/java in
  package org.invoicer. DO NOT modify anything under invoicer/src/test or pettycash/src/test: the specifications are
  the operators', and if one fails, the code is what is wrong. Keep every class either project already has exactly as
  it is.

subGoals.description:
A new project, adopted as it stands. Its tree holds only its build file (pom.xml), a README, and the
  operator's specification under src/test/java; nothing exists under src/main/java yet. In its own words,
  from its README:

    "invoicer -- Invoices in one currency: money with its currency, billing periods, invoice lines and their
    total."

  It is a library, in package org.invoicer, with no dependencies beyond the JDK.

  - Money is a record of an amount in cents (long cents) and a currency (String currency): three upper-case
    letters, else IllegalArgumentException.
  - Money.parse(String) reads "<decimal> <currency>": a decimal with at most two places and an optional
    leading '-' ("12.50 EUR" is 1250 cents in EUR, "0.5 CHF" is 50), one space, the currency. Anything else
    raises IllegalArgumentException.
  - plus(Money) adds two amounts of the same currency (another currency raises IllegalArgumentException);
    times(int n) multiplies. toString() prints two places and the currency: "12.50 EUR", "-0.05 USD".
  - Period is a record of a first and a last day (LocalDate from, LocalDate to), from not after to, else
    IllegalArgumentException. contains(LocalDate) is true from the first to the last day inclusive; days()
    returns how many days it spans, both ends included (a long).
  - LineItem is a record of a description (not blank), a quantity (int, positive) and a unit price (Money),
    else IllegalArgumentException; amount() is the unit price times the quantity.
  - Invoice is a class constructed with a number (String), a period (Period) and a currency (String).
    addLine(LineItem) adds a line whose unit price is in the invoice's currency, else raises
    IllegalArgumentException and adds nothing. lines() returns the lines in the order added, as a List that
    cannot be modified. total() is the sum of the lines' amounts, zero in the invoice's currency when there
    are none. number() and period() return what it was constructed with.

  The specification is InvoicerSpecTest in src/test/java: its tests say exactly what the library must
  return, and they fail until the code provides it.

  OBJECTIVE: every test in InvoicerSpecTest passes, and the whole suite passes.

  The classes to change are Money, Period, LineItem and Invoice -- none exists yet: create them under
  src/main/java in package org.invoicer. DO NOT modify anything under src/test: the specification is the
  operator's, and if one of its tests fails, the code is what is wrong.

subGoals.description:
A new project, adopted as it stands. Its tree holds only its build file (pom.xml), a README, and the
  operator's specification under src/test/java; nothing exists under src/main/java yet. In its own words,
  from its README:

    "pettycash -- A petty-cash book: amounts in cents, expenses with a payee, a category and whether they are
    billable, totals by category and period."

  It is a library, in package org.pettycash, with no dependencies beyond the JDK.

  - Amount is a record of an amount in cents (long cents). Amount.parse(String) reads a decimal with at most
    two places and an optional leading '-' ("12.50" is 1250, "0.5" is 50); anything else raises
    IllegalArgumentException. plus(Amount) adds, negate() changes the sign, toString() prints two places:
    "12.50", "-0.05".
  - Period is a record of a first and a last day (LocalDate from, LocalDate to), from not after to, else
    IllegalArgumentException. contains(LocalDate) is true from the first to the last day inclusive; days()
    returns how many days it spans, both ends included (a long).
  - Category is an enum: FOOD, TRAVEL, OFFICE, OTHER, in that order.
  - Expense is a record of a date (LocalDate), a payee (String, not blank), an amount (Amount, positive), a
    category (Category) and whether it is billable (boolean billable), else IllegalArgumentException.
  - ExpenseBook is a class with a no-argument constructor. add(Expense) adds an expense at the end;
    expenses() returns them in that order, as a List that cannot be modified; total() is the sum of their
    amounts and totalFor(Category) the sum of one category's (zero when there are none); within(Period)
    lists the expenses whose date the period contains, and billable() the billable ones, both in order.

  The specification is PettyCashSpecTest in src/test/java: its tests say exactly what the library must
  return, and they fail until the code provides it.

  OBJECTIVE: every test in PettyCashSpecTest passes, and the whole suite passes.

  The classes to change are Amount, Period, Category, Expense and ExpenseBook -- none exists yet: create them
  under src/main/java in package org.pettycash. DO NOT modify anything under src/test: the specification is
  the operator's, and if one of its tests fails, the code is what is wrong.

subGoals.description: Implement the Amount record in package org.pettycash with a long cents field, a static parse(String) that reads a decimal with at most two places and an optional leading '-', plus(Amount), negate(), and a two-place toString()

acceptanceCriteria: Amount.parse("12.50") yields an amount whose toString() is "12.50"
Amount.parse("0.5") yields an amount whose toString() is "0.50"
Amount.parse("-0.05") yields an amount whose toString() is "-0.05"
Amount.parse("12.5") yields an amount whose toString() is "12.50"
Amount.parse("12.50") plus Amount.parse("0.50") yields an amount whose toString() is "13.00"
Amount.parse("12.50") plus Amount.parse("-0.50") yields an amount whose toString() is "12.00"
Amount.parse("12.50") plus Amount.parse("-12.50") yields an amount whose toString() is "0.00"
Amount.parse("12.50") plus Amount.parse("-13.00") yields an amount whose toString() is "-0.50"
Amount.parse("12.50").negate() yields an amount whose toString() is "-12.50"
Amount.parse("-12.50").negate() yields an amount whose toString() is "12.50"
Amount.parse("0.00").negate() yields an amount whose toString() is "0.00"
